passages.original: XII. Tractoriae nomine quid intelligatur.—Tractu- riae seu tractoriae, vel tractatoriae vocabulum, quo do- natur haec epistola, et in quo exprimendo eadem apud Augustinum est veterum codicum varietas, ad ecclesiasticum usum a jure civili translatum fuit. In Codice Theod. lib. VIII, specialis est titulus 6, de tractoriis et stativis, ubi tractoria id est quod epistola, qua castrensibus muniis absoluti domum dimitteban- tur, ut etiam liquet ex lib.
passages.english: XII. What is to be understood by the name *tractoria*.—The word *tracturia* or *tractoria*, or *tractatoria*, by which this letter is designated, and in rendering which the same variation among the old manuscripts is found in Augustine, was transferred to ecclesiastical usage from civil law. In the Theodosian Code, book VIII, there is a special title 6, "On *tractoriae* and *stativae*", where a *tractoria* is the same as the letter by which those released from military duties were sent home, as is also clear from book
passages.notes: Scanning hyphenations (Tractu- riae, do- natur, dimitteban- tur) have been joined. *Tractoria* (a letter of authorisation or summons) and *stativae* (postings or stations) are kept as technical terms. The sentence breaks off at "from book"; the following context gives the reference as VII, title 18, law 11.

passages.original: 8, litteras inlelligit per totum orbem terrarum missas super eorum nomine qui vel fuerint convicti, vel de objectis criminibus respondere pertinaciter noluerint. Eodem intellectu Marius Mercator in Commonit. Tractoriam appellat Zosimi epistolam de Pelagii et Coelestii damnatione omnibus ecclesiis inscriptam.
passages.english: 8, he understands [by it] letters sent throughout the whole world concerning the names of those who either had been convicted, or had stubbornly refused to answer the charges brought against them. In the same sense Marius Mercator, in the Commonitorium, calls the letter of Zosimus on the condemnation of Pelagius and Caelestius, addressed to all the churches, a Tractoria.
passages.notes: The passage begins mid-sentence, continuing a reference to Augustine, epist. 43, n. 8 (see preceding context). 'inlelligit' is a scanning error for 'intelligit'. Tractoria/Tractatoria is a technical term for a circular or synodical letter, kept untranslated.
